title: IdP adapter compatibility playbook and edge-case runbook (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, PingFederate)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a hands-on playbook and developer-runbook for the IdP adapters used by Redwood's SSO layer so that RBAC v2 role bindings, audit logging, and admin controls behave reliably across Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and PingFederate. This ticket consolidates observed quirks, test cases, mitigation patterns, and rollout steps for each IdP and produces a single consumable doc plus test harness artifacts.
background: During early Private and Dedicated customer integrations we saw multiple IdP-specific failures: group overflow in Azure, claim name mismatches in Google Workspace, Okta sending groups as separate assertions vs claims depending on SCIM enabled, and PingFederate audience/cert rollover edge cases. These caused RBAC v2 role binding mismatches and noisy audit logs. We need a canonical playbook for engineering and solutions to follow when onboarding customers and to bake into the console's IdP configuration UI hints.
compatibility_matrix_summary: High-level compatibility: Okta (full SAML + OIDC + SCIM) - best coverage but multiple attribute formats; Azure AD (SAML/OIDC + groups overage handling) - watch group overage and claims mapping; Google Workspace (SAML + SCIM limited) - uses 'memberOf' / custom attributes for groups; PingFederate (enterprise-grade SAML) - flexible assertions but common audience and NameID pitfalls. Recommended default mappings and fallback rules are in idp_notes below.
idp_notes: Okta: Prefer 'groups' SAML attribute when SCIM is not available. Watch for URL-encoded group names with slashes. Okta may issue multiple <AttributeStatement> blocks; our parser must aggregate all group attributes across statements. Default NameID formats: persistent or email - accept both but normalize to lowercase email for RBAC matching.

Azure AD: Large tenant group lists may be omitted from SAML and replaced with a 'groups' claim that contains an opaque id set. Implement group-overflow detection (presence of 'hasgroups' or 'groups' omitted) and fall back to SCIM or Azure's Graph API if available. Azure may return groups as GUIDs; map GUID->group-name via a provisioning sync or on-demand lookup during initial login.

Google Workspace: Uses 'memberOf' or custom group attribute; customers often put groups into a custom SAML attribute named 'groups' or 'http://schemas.google.com/claims/groups'. Google may include domain-qualified emails as group identifiers; implement parsing rules to strip domain if mapping expects short names. NameID is frequently 'email'; prefer that for admin account detection.

PingFederate: Highly configurable; common failures are audience mismatch and certificate rollover without automated metadata fetch. Recommend enabling metadata URL and validating entityID/audience against our SP entity. For high-security tenants, provide an option to accept multiple certificates and show certificate fingerprint in Console.

General mapping rules: 1) Normalize all incoming group/role strings to unicode NFC and lower-case; 2) Strip common prefixes like 'CN=' or domain qualifiers when mapping; 3) Support both group-name and group-id bindings in RBAC v2; 4) If attribute-based role mapping is used, allow admins to supply a mapping table in Console and persist a verification sample assertion for troubleshooting.

Audit logging implications: Log both raw SAML attributes and normalized role bindings. For privacy, redact PII where required but keep deterministic hashes for debugging. Emit structured audit events for: assertion_received, attribute_mapping_applied, role_binding_resolved, provisioning_fallback_invoked, and idp_cert_rollover_detected.

Admin controls: Provide Console toggles for: 'treat NameID as admin if in list', 'enable group GUID->name lookup', 'allow multiple certs', and 'fallback to SCIM/Graph on group overflow'. Each toggle should be recorded in admin audit logs when changed.
test_plan: Unit tests: parser should aggregate multiple AttributeStatements and preserve duplicate group entries but deduplicate before RBAC mapping.
Integration tests: create test tenants per IdP that exercise: normal group assertions, group overflow (Azure), escaped characters (Okta), custom attribute names (Google), cert rollover (Ping).

E2E test harness: scripted SAML responses stored in test fixtures (okta_saml_sample_escaped.xml, azure_overflow.xml, google_custom_attribute.xml, ping_cert_rollover.xml) and run through test instance of our SP. Verify final role assignments and audit events.

Load test: simulate authentication bursts (1000 logins/min) to validate that assertion parsing doesn't create hotspots or disk IO; ensure audit log aggregator can ingest assertion metadata at expected RPS.

Manual QA: checklist for solutions engineers when onboarding customer: capture an example SAMLResponse, request metadata URL, verify group format, document expected mapping in customer onboarding ticket.
Security tests: ensure SAML signatures validated against IdP cert, enforce audience and recipient checks, reject expired assertions and log reason with assertion id for traceability.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Merge parser updates behind feature flag idp_adapter_v2; enable for internal staging tenants and two low-risk customers per IdP. Monitor errors and audit events for 72 hours.
Phase 2 (wider internal): Enable for all internal accounts and Redwood-managed demo tenants. Collect additional mappings to enrich heuristics and update mapping table.

Phase 3 (gradual customer opt-in): Add Console toggle 'Use improved IdP adapter' for customer enablement and advise Solutions team to opt in during onboarding. Provide rollback button tied to feature flag.
Phase 4 (GA): Flip default to enabled for new customers, notify existing customers by email and Console banner, run migration job for stored role bindings if mapping semantics changed.

Rollback criteria: >1% of active users failing to map roles after 24h or any P0 incident involving admin lockout. In that case, automatically flip feature flag off and surface affected tenants in a runbook dashboard.
Post-rollout: schedule a security review and a run of the audit-logging retention sanity check to ensure no sensitive PII persisted in plain text.
acceptance_criteria: Parser aggregates AttributeStatement blocks and passes unit tests for all fixture files.
RBAC v2 role bindings created from assertions match expected fixtures for all four IdP test tenants.
Audit pipeline logs structured events for attribute mapping and role resolution and can be queried by assertion id.
Console exposes the four admin toggles with audit events recorded on change.
Feature flag rollout path validated and rollback worked in staging within 15 minutes.
Security review completed and signed-off by Security team (link in attachments).
observability: Dashboard: SSO > IdP Adapter Errors (counts by idp, reason) - https://internal.redwood/dashboards/sso/idp-adapter-errors
Alert: idp_adapter_high_error_rate - triggers at 0.5% error rate sustained for 15m
